question: An open-ended prompt like "improve this codebase" is run against the Agent SDK without any turn or budget limits, and the session runs far longer and costs far more than expected. For their next production deployment, the team wants the loop to stop automatically once either a turn count or a dollar amount is exceeded, and to be able to tell which limit was hit from the final message. What should they configure and check?
options: A) Set effort to "low", since lower reasoning effort automatically caps the number of turns a session can take before the agent loop terminates on its own.
B) Set max_turns and max_budget_usd in ClaudeAgentOptions, then check the ResultMessage subtype, error_max_turns or error_max_budget_usd, to see which limit fired.
C) Set permission_mode to "dontAsk", since denying every unmatched tool call causes the loop to terminate once no further tools remain available to try.
D) Poll total_cost_usd after every turn and manually call an abort method once a threshold is crossed, since the SDK offers no built-in way to cap turns or spend at all.
correct_answers: B) Set max_turns and max_budget_usd in ClaudeAgentOptions, then check the ResultMessage subtype, error_max_turns or error_max_budget_usd, to see which limit fired.
explanations: effort controls how much reasoning Claude applies per turn and its associated token cost, not a hard limit on the total number of turns a session can take.

Correct. max_turns and max_budget_usd are the documented options for capping the loop, and when either limit is hit the SDK returns a ResultMessage whose subtype is error_max_turns or error_max_budget_usd so the caller can tell which one fired.

dontAsk changes whether unmatched tool calls are denied instead of prompted; it does not impose any cap on the number of turns or the amount spent, and Claude can still keep producing text-only turns indefinitely.
The SDK already provides built-in max_turns and max_budget_usd options for exactly this purpose, so manually polling cost and aborting externally is unnecessary.
